newsitem.title: KENYA: Hundreds of students demonstrate in Nairobi.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of students demonstrate in Nairobi.

text.p: Hundreds of Kenyan students streamed into the city centre on Wednesday in response to a call for more protests by opposition groups demanding constitutional reforms, witnesses said.

The Nairobi University demonstrators were apparently angered by a report in the independent Daily Nation newspaper that four students had died of wounds in clashes with police during protests on Monday.
If the Daily Nation report is confirmed, it would bring the death toll from Monday's violence across Kenya to 13.

The students blocked the main highway through the Kenyan capital at the height of the morning rush hour. Riot police and elite paramilitary General Service Unit (GSU) personnel moved in to confront the students.
More police reinforcements headed for the main university campus close to State House, President Daniel arap Moi's official residence, where a regional heads of state summit was taking place.
Nine people were killed in Kenya on Monday during the most violent clashes between police and protesters since unrest in 1991 that helped push Moi to allow multi-party elections.

Opposition parties, human rights groups and other bodies under the umbrella National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC) have called for protests on Wednesday to press the government for constitutional reforms before elections.
The parties said they would demonstrate at State House to bring Kenya to the attention of visiting leaders from Sudan, Uganda, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti who are discussing the conflict in Sudan.

"Kenya needs conflict management just like Sudan. As a country we don't have the moral authority to tell others how to manage conflict. We will demonstrate, go to where these leaders are meeting, and tell them these things," NCEC core convenor Kivutha Kibwana said on Tuesday.

Kenyan officials ridiculed the opposition's ability to disrupt President Daniel arap Moi's six-nation summit, which opened at State House on Tuesday and closes on Wednesday morning. They said they expected protest calls to go unheeded.
More than 100 Nairobi University students marched out of their campus late on Tuesday and stoned cars in more than two hours of protest.
They blocked traffic on the main highway through Nairobi until about 70 riot and elite paramilitary General Service Unit police pushed them back, firing baton rounds and teargas.

Later, residents of Nairobi's exclusive Riverside Drive neighbourhood said they heard firing after students again broke out of their residences and police reservists blocked the road into the area. It was unclear what was happening.
London-based human rights group Amnesty International deplored Monday's police violence and said those responsible should be brought to justice.

"Excessive violence was clearly used in an attempt to intimidate pro-democracy activists from holding further rallies," Amnesty International said on Tuesday, adding that constitutional reforms after elections would be meaningless.

Reformists want the repeal of six laws that date from colonial times including the Public Order Act used to regulate public gatherings. They are also demanding free access to state-controlled media, particularly radio, and changes in the electoral law.
The NCEC called for three days of national mourning from Wednesday to Friday for those killed on Monday.

It said it was planning a national strike and holding protests outside provincial administration centres as part of its non-violent campaign to force constitutional changes, which Moi says cannot be introduced before the general election.
No date has been set for the parliamentary and presidential polls in which Moi, 73, is still widely expected to win another five-year term because of squabbling among oppositon leaders.

"We expect the forthcoming election to be conducted without violence so the Kenyan people can express their democratic verdict. The events over the weekend are yet one further serious blow to that process," British Foreign Office minister Tony Lloyd told parliament on Tuesday.
